text:
Eli: hey team, ran into a weird onboarding quirk. used Migration Assistant to move data from my personal MBP to the company M2 and Kandji enrollment mostly worked, but FileVault shows a personal recovery key and Kandji says "escrow mismatch". Login name also shows my old shortname. stuck on a couple prompts. any tips?
rory-it: hi Eli, welcome — quick clarifying q: did you sign into the new Mac with the company invite account or with your personal Apple ID during setup?
Eli: i signed into the company invite, but Migration Assistant brought over the user account from my personal Mac (same shortname). so it looks like the local user UID+home were copied. Kandji device appears enrolled under the asset tag but user binding is odd.
kate-kandji: Kandji here — that pattern happens when the migrated local account already has FileVault enabled with a personal protector. Kandji expects an MDM-enrolled user flow (MDM creates managed admin, escrows key). Can you paste output of `id -u` and `sudo fdesetup status`?
Eli: posted quick copy:
```bash
$ id -u
501

$ sudo fdesetup status
FileVault is On.
Users: eli (Enabled)
Escrow: Personal recovery key present (non-institutional)
```
Eli: Kandji UI shows enrollment OK but the owner field is blank and the "claimed by" email is the asset owner, not the login user.
rory-it: thanks. two safe options: 1) create a new, fresh managed admin user (company email) and migrate your files into that account — preserves data and ensures MDM-first FileVault protector; or 2) IT can remove the personal protector and trigger Kandji to push institutional escrow (we'll need a temp-admin session). Which do you prefer?
Eli: i'd prefer not to re-copy everything if possible. what are the tradeoffs?
alex-sec: security note: leaving a personal protector on a corporate device is not allowed — it prevents us from reliably key escrow and recovery. Option 2 is ok if done immediately under IT supervision so we log key operations. Option 1 is cleaner long-term because the user principal is correct and avoids odd permission remnants from Migration Assistant.
erin-people: looping in onboarding so we track whichever path you choose. :white_check_mark: Eli i'll mark this on your checklist.
kate-kandji: if you pick option 2 we'll do: temp-admin session, remove the personal recovery protector, force Kandji to push the institutional key, verify with `sudo fdesetup status`, then have you re-register any hardware keys. If escrow fails we fall back to reprovision.
rory-it: If you want minimal downtime, option 2 is faster (10-20m). Option 1 requires creating a managed admin, copying data (rsync) and fixing permissions — can be 1-2 hours depending on home dir size.
Eli: ok temp-admin route works for me. i'm at my desk now and have a USB-C hub.
deploy-bot: temp-admin session created for rory-it (25m). ticket ONB-5234.
rory-it: prepping now. Eli please confirm you have a backup of any SSH keys in ~/.ssh and your ~/.gnupg exported if you use it. we'll remove the personal protector on disk-level, not touch file contents.
Eli: confirmed i backed up SSH keys and GPG. ready.
rory-it: done — removed personal protector and forced Kandji keyset push. confirm status:```bash
$ sudo fdesetup status
FileVault is On.
Users: eli (Enabled)
Escrow: Institutional recovery key present (Kandji)
```
Eli: saw that — restarted and FileVault unlock accepted my account password. logging in now. everything looks fine, and my home dir permissions unchanged. thanks!
kate-kandji: I'll keep monitoring the device for a couple check-ins to ensure the institutional key is persisted across reboots.
alex-sec: please re-register any second-factor tokens in SSO so device login and admin flows remain consistent.
erin-people: noted and closing onboarding item when you confirm SSO 2FA.
Eli: confirmed re-registered OK. appreciate the help and the clear steps — will avoid running Migration Assistant next time until after MDM enrollment. :thumbsup:
rory-it: filing a short note for procurement/IT docs about Migration Assistant edge-case so future new hires get a recommended flow.
